adjustments: sec. 911(a) foreign earned income exclusion denied

issues.question: Other (sec. 911 foreign earned income exclusion): Is petitioner a qualified individual (physical presence 330 days and foreign tax home/abode) entitled to exclude his 2016 Saudi Arabia wages?
issues.holding: Yes; physical presence test met (at least 330 full days abroad in 2016) and abode/tax home in Saudi Arabia; wages excludable up to the sec. 911(b)(2) limitation

amount_determined.description: exclusion limited by sec. 911(b)(2); computed under Rule 155

issues.computable_reason: Physical presence day count is mechanical (21 or 25 U.S. days), but the abode/tax home element is a facts-and-circumstances weighing of domestic ties

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for sec. 6651(a)(1) and (a)(2) additions to tax for 2016?
issues.holding: Liable; no return filed by April 15, 2017; SFR treated as return for (a)(2); no reasonable cause; additions computed on tax as redetermined (pension income and wages above the exclusion limit remain taxable)

amount_determined.description: additions computed on redetermined tax under Rule 155

issues.computable_reason: No return filed, SFR exists, no reasonable cause argued; amounts are statutory percentages of redetermined tax

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Foreign earned income exclusion allowed (physical presence and Saudi abode) up to sec. 911(b)(2) limit; pension income remains taxable; 6651(a)(1) and (a)(2) additions sustained on redetermined tax; 6654 and COD income conceded by respondent

notes: Some facts stipulated; burden on petitioner. Court skipped bona fide residence analysis. Pension income is not foreign earned income (sec. 911(b)(1)(B)(i)). Annual exclusion limit for 2016 not stated in opinion. Additions amounts not stated.
